name: Saffire IV, V and VI
facility: Saffire flow unit in the Cygnus cabin (about 17-19 m3)
objective: Burn large samples at reduced pressure and raised oxygen and measure heat release, gas products and smoke detection in a spacecraft-sized volume
materials: SIBAL cotton-fiberglass cloth, cotton jersey, PMMA slabs (one-sided, two-sided, ribbed)
geometry: Samples up to 50 cm long; PMMA slabs 18 cm
variables: Material, O2 and pressure (cabin atmosphere), flow cut from 20 to 5 cm/s in one test
sensors: O2 for oxygen-consumption calorimetry, CO2, CO, temperatures at the flow unit and far field, smoke detection, video
in_burnbook: 5 large-scale tests with heat release and cabin CO/CO2 rise
sources: Urban et al. 2024 Saffire VI ICES presentation; Eigenbrod et al. 2021 ICES-2021-218

name: Saffire-II
objective: Burn nine small samples of different spacecraft materials in microgravity and compare with the same materials burned on the ground
materials: Silicone sheets, SIBAL cotton-fiberglass, PMMA, PMMA joined to Nomex
geometry: 29 x 5 cm strips, 0.27 mm to about 1 cm thick
variables: Material and thickness; flow direction for one sample
sensors: Thermocouples (flow duct inlet and outlet, embedded in the sample, plume); 4 radiometers (2 front, 2 back); solid-state CO2, O2 and pressure sensors in the avionics bay; anemometers on each side of the sample; 2 cameras; smoke wire for flow uniformity
in_burnbook: 9 samples with microgravity and 1g burn results; sensor records (pressure, O2, CO2, radiometers, thermocouples) for samples 1, 5, 7 and 9
sources: NASA PSI table PSI-99; Space.com 2016; SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III description of data (PSI), Table 2; Saffire-II sample 1 sensor workbook (PSI)
unknowns: Pressure is the sample 1 sensor mean (14.866 psia, steady within 0.04 psia on 21 Nov 2016); samples 5, 7 and 9 read 14.88 to 14.91 psia. The igniter voltage channel in this file is not physical (about 762 V), so igniter power comes from the PSI table

name: Saffire-I
objective: First large spacecraft fire test: how fast a large fire grows in low gravity and whether it reaches a steady spread rate
materials: SIBAL cotton-fiberglass cloth
geometry: 0.4 m wide x 0.94 m long sheet
sensors: Thermocouples (flow duct inlet and outlet, embedded in the sample, plume); 4 radiometers (2 front, 2 back); solid-state CO2, O2 and pressure sensors in the avionics bay; anemometers on each side of the sample; 2 cameras; smoke wire for flow uniformity
in_burnbook: 2 burns with burn times; sample 2 sensor record (pressure, O2, CO2, radiometers, thermocouples) at 1 s
sources: NASA PSI table PSI-98; Ruff and Urban 2016; SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III description of data (PSI), Table 2; Saffire-I sample 2 sensor workbook (PSI)
unknowns: Pressure is the sample 2 sensor mean (14.877 psia, varying under 0.03 psia); sample 1's sensor file is not yet in BurnBook. The O2 sensor read about 22.3% while the PSI table lists 21.5-21.7%. No CO sensor on Saffire-I

name: Saffire-III
objective: Repeat the Saffire-I burn at 30 cm/s to see how air speed changes how fast a large fire grows
materials: SIBAL cotton-fiberglass cloth
geometry: 0.4 m wide x 0.94 m long sheet
sensors: Thermocouples (flow duct inlet and outlet, embedded in the sample, plume); 4 radiometers (2 front, 2 back); solid-state CO2, O2 and pressure sensors in the avionics bay; anemometers on each side of the sample; 2 cameras; smoke wire for flow uniformity
in_burnbook: Sample 1 sensor record (pressure, O2, CO2, radiometers, thermocouples; /api/saffire/sensors?record=saffire3_s1) plus vehicle telemetry for both burns (cabin pressure, temperature, smoke detector; record saffire3)
sources: NASA PSI table PSI-100; Spaceflight101 OA-7 report; SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III description of data (PSI), Table 2; Saffire-III telemetry workbook (NASA PSI); Saffire-III sample 1 sensor workbook (NASA PSI)
unknowns: Pressure is Saffire's sensor (14.46 psia); the Cygnus cabin sensors read 13.99 psia (96.4 kPa), unresolved. O2 sensor read 19.8%, low for cabin air. No sensor workbook for sample 2 (opposed), only 30 s telemetry; PSI's Saffire-III data records otherwise hold camera image sets. No CO sensor. No burn lengths or spread rates in PSI-100. Anemometers read about 24 to 25 cm/s versus 30 cm/s listed

name: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids II)
facility: Microgravity Science Glovebox, SPICE flow duct
objective: Measure how solid materials ignite, spread and go out under spacecraft-like ventilation at reduced oxygen
materials: PMMA rods, films, slabs and spherical sections; SIBAL fabric; Nomex; wax candle
geometry: Rods 6.35-12.7 mm, sheets 0.1-5 mm, 4 cm spherical section, 1-2 cm fabric strips
variables: O2 (N2 dilution), flow speed and direction, sample thickness and diameter
sensors: O2 and CO (CSA-CP), CO2 (CDM), thermopile radiometer, video with flow overlay, Nikon D300s still camera, airspeed transducer
in_burnbook: 129 tests with O2/CO2/CO, air speed and outcome flags; summary report findings
sources: NASA/TM-20210011385 (BASS-II Summary Report); NASA PSI table PSI-25

name: BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids)
facility: Microgravity Science Glovebox, SPICE flow duct
objective: Examine burning and extinction of solid fuels in microgravity to guide fire-safety models
materials: PMMA spheres and slabs, SIBAL fabric, Nomex, Ultem, wax candles and slabs
geometry: 1 and 2 cm PMMA spheres, slabs, flat samples
variables: O2 (21% down to 17%), flow speed, nitrogen as a suppressant
sensors: Not in our sources (same duct and cameras as BASS-II)
sources: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); NASA PSI table PSI-26
unknowns: Per-test O2, flow and outcomes not in the PSI table; pressure assumed at glovebox (cabin) pressure

name: Drop-tower flammability tests (Olson 2008)
platform: NASA Glenn 5.18 s Zero Gravity Research Facility
objective: Compare microgravity flammability with NASA's standard upward-burn test and correlate thin-fuel flame spread
materials: Kimwipes cellulose, Nomex, Ultem, Mylar
in_burnbook: Spread-rate model (22 tests) and flammability limits for 3 fuels
sources: Olson et al. 2008 NASA/TM-2008-215260
unknowns: O2 range shown is the Kimwipes correlation range; the 5.18 s test time limits how long a flame can be watched

name: Discrete fuel spread (Carney 2021)
objective: Find when a flame can jump the gaps between separate pieces of fuel
materials: Cellulose (TENGU paper)
sources: Carney et al. 2021

name: SAME / SAME-R (Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment)
objective: Measure the size of smoke particles from overheated spacecraft materials, to design better smoke detectors
materials: Spacecraft materials heated to smoke (no flame)
sources: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); NIST and NASA SAME reports
unknowns: No SAME data in BurnBook yet; attributes not filled

name: ACME BRE (Burning Rate Emulator)
objective: Imitate a burning solid with a gas burner to measure burning and self-extinction at raised oxygen and reduced pressure
materials: Methane and ethylene, pure or N2-diluted
variables: O2 and pressure as paired atmospheres (14.7 psia/21%, 10.2 psia/26.5%, 8.2 psia/34%, and about 1 atm at 25-40%), fuel (ethylene or methane, pure or 50% N2), fuel mass flux, burner size
sensors: Two heat-flux gauges and a copper calorimeter in the burner surface, burner surface thermocouples, radiometer array (often saturated), chamber pressure transducer, fuel and N2 mass flow controllers, colour video, OH* and CH* chemiluminescence, thin-filament pyrometry (mostly round 2), gas chromatograph between tests
in_burnbook: 18 test days (fuel, O2 levels, flames lit); tested atmospheres and headline results from the BRE final report
sources: Stocker 2021 (NTRS 20210021781); NASA PSI table PSI-20; ACME/BRE Final Report, Stocker, Quintiere, Sunderland, de Ris and Dehghani (NASA GRC, 1 Feb 2022)
unknowns: Pressure, fuel flow and outcome for each flame are not tabulated (only in PSI raw data); day-level table sums to 194 flames, report text says 196 ignitions; most round-2 tests at about 14.7 psia

name: CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases)
objective: Find when hot gas flames turn into cool flames and how long flames last across oxygen and pressure
materials: Ethane, propane, butane (some diluted)
variables: Fuel, dilution, fuel flow, chamber O2 and pressure; normal and inverse flames (inverse up to 85% O2 through the burner)
sensors: Thin-filament pyrometry, photomultiplier, burner temperature, intensified camera (formaldehyde filter)
sources: NASA PSI table PSI-159; Stocker 2021 (NTRS 20210021781); CFI-G test-day tables (Increments 64-66, normal and inverse flames)
unknowns: Test-day tables state the atmosphere is nominal: pressure rises and O2 falls with vitiation during a day, which matches the drifting O2 in the per-test table

name: SPICE (Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment)
facility: Microgravity Science Glovebox, SPICE flow duct
objective: Find the largest gas-jet flame that does not shed soot (the smoke point)
materials: Methane, ethane, ethylene, propane, propylene blends
geometry: Round burners 0.76-3.2 mm in air coflow
variables: Fuel, burner diameter, fuel flow, coflow speed
sensors: Video with flow overlay, radiometer, fuel mass flow controller
in_burnbook: 11 published ethylene smoke points and 16 measured video frames
sources: DeBold 2012 thesis (Univ. of Maryland); NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)
unknowns: Only ethylene, 1.6 mm burner, loaded so far

name: ACME CLD Flame (Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame)
objective: Measure soot and lift-off in coflow flames of diluted fuels
materials: Methane and ethylene diluted with nitrogen
variables: Fuel and dilution, fuel and nitrogen flow
in_burnbook: 32 test days (fuel, concentration range, flames lit)
sources: Stocker 2021 (NTRS 20210021781); NASA PSI table PSI-21; Cao et al. 2018, Combust. Theory Model. 22:316 (ground study)
unknowns: Pressure and coflow speed on the ISS are not in the PSI table. A ground study by the same group (Cao, Smooke et al. 2018) burned nitrogen-diluted methane coflow flames at 1.0 to 2.7 atm with 35 cm/s coflow in normal gravity; those are lab conditions, not the ISS ones, so they are not used here

name: ACME Flame Design
objective: Find conditions that make flames burn without soot
materials: Ethylene with oxygen at several concentrations
variables: Reactant flow, ambient O2; normal and inverse flames
unknowns: O2 values and test table not in BurnBook

name: ACME E-FIELD Flames
objective: See how electric fields push on flames; the closest thing in the data to a body force like partial gravity
materials: Methane and ethylene, pure and diluted
geometry: Gas-jet and coflow burners; fields up to 10 kV
variables: Electric field strength, fuel and dilution

name: ACME s-Flame
objective: Measure the structure and extinction of spherical flames to test combustion models
materials: Hydrogen, methane, ethylene, diluted with nitrogen or helium
unknowns: No s-Flame data in BurnBook yet

name: SLICE (Structure and Liftoff in Combustion Experiment)
objective: Study how gas-jet flames lift off the burner, to improve combustion models
materials: Methane diluted with nitrogen (40, 70 and 100% CH4 by mole)
geometry: Coflow burner: 3.24 mm fuel tube inside a 7.62 cm square air duct
variables: Fuel dilution and fuel jet speed (about 24 to 89 cm/s); each flame also run in 1 g
sensors: Digital SLR colour camera, calibrated as a ratio pyrometer for soot temperature
in_burnbook: Headline results for 18 ISS flames from Cao et al. 2015
sources: Cao, Ma, Bennett, Giassi, Stocker, Takahashi, Long and Smooke, Proc. Combust. Inst. 35 (2015) 897-903
unknowns: Cabin or glovebox pressure and the coflow air speed are not stated as numbers (a fitted coflow profile is shown); no PSI table loaded

name: FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment)
facility: Combustion Integrated Rack, Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus
objective: Measure how inert-gas suppressants (CO2, helium, xenon) change the flammability limits of fuel droplets
materials: Methanol (first phase), then n-heptane droplets
variables: Fuel (methanol, n-heptane), droplet diameter (1.1 to 4.7 mm), O2 (12 to 34% by mole), pressure (about 0.7, 1, 2 and 3 atm), diluent (N2, CO2 up to 70%, He up to 45%)
sensors: Color camera and low-light UV camera (flame and droplet diameter)
in_burnbook: 274 ISS droplet tests with gas mix, pressure, droplet and extinction size, burning rate, burn time and how each test ended
sources: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); ASGSR 28th Annual Meeting slide 'ISS FLEX MeOH Test Results' (Dynamics of Water Absorption and Evaporation During Methanol Droplet Combustion in Microgravity, slide 11); Farouk and Dryer 2013, Isolated Alkane Droplet Combustion in Microgravity: Cool Flames (8th U.S. National Combustion Meeting); PSI FLEX heptane test plot FLEX-242 (H04H201, 27 Sep 2011); NASA PSI table PSI-69 (FLEX experimental table)
unknowns: 32 rows have values marked as not measured; one pressure recorded as 0; one identifier listed twice. Fraction burned depends on droplet size as well as gas mix, so group comparisons need similar starting sizes

name: FLEX-2
facility: Combustion Integrated Rack, Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus
objective: Extend FLEX to practical fuels and mixtures, soot formation and droplet-droplet interactions
materials: Per PSI-68: iso-octane, n-octane, n-heptane, n-decane, ethanol; mixtures 1-propanol/glycerol (95/5 and 80/20), n-heptane/iso-octane (50/50)
geometry: Droplets 1.5 to 5.0 mm on a support fiber or free; binary droplet arrays
variables: Fuel and fuel mixture, O2 mole fraction (0.17, 0.21, 0.25, 0.30), pressure (0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3 atm), diluent (N2 or He), droplet size 1.5 to 5 mm, slow flow 0.1 to 5 cm/s by moving the droplet; droplet spacing in the SRD
sensors: Back-lit droplet camera, OH* flame imaging, colour flame camera, thermopile radiometers (broad-band and 1.87 um water band), soot volume fraction, multi-wavelength soot and fiber pyrometry, chamber temperature and pressure
sources: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); FLEX-2 Science Requirements Document, Rev. 1 (Williams et al., 15 March 2010), Table 2 and sections 5.1-5.2; NASA PSI table PSI-68 (FLEX-2)
unknowns: Both PSI-68 and the 2010 SRD list the planned matrix (values joined by "or"), not the conditions flown; the SRD envelope is wider (10 to 40% O2) and its fuel list differs (n-hexadecane and n-propylbenzene mixtures, no iso-octane or n-octane). Per-test conditions and results are not in BurnBook. Years not in our sources

name: CFI (Cool Flames Investigation)
facility: Combustion Integrated Rack, Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (FLEX hardware)
objective: Follow-up to FLEX and FLEX-2: study quasi-steady cool flames around fuel droplets, and how fuel structure, pressure and helium dilution change them (distinct from CFI-G, which uses gases)
materials: n-dodecane; n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures (75/25 and 60/40 by mass); farnesane (renewable jet fuel)
geometry: Droplets about 4 mm, free-floating or on a 40 micron silicon-carbide fiber
variables: Fuel and fuel mixture, pressure (0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 2, 3, 5 atm), helium dilution (29% and 59%), O2 (21% and 17%), fiber-supported or free droplet
sensors: Backlit black-and-white camera (droplet size), UV camera for OH* emission (flame size), colour camera, narrow-band and wide-band radiometers
in_burnbook: All 227 tests (FLEX-1206 to 1431): conditions for every test; droplet and extinction sizes, burning rates, re-ignitions, radiation and crew comments for the 146 analysed (farnesane not yet analysed)
sources: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); NASA Space Apps mission brief; Nayagam and Dietrich 2020, Cool Flame Investigation (CFI) Science Final Report; NASA PSI table PSI-39 (CFI); CFI data summary spreadsheet (NASA, January 2021)
unknowns: Farnesane tests (FLEX-1388 to 1431) are listed but not analysed. The report states objectives over 0.25 to 5 atm; the lowest test run is 0.5 atm. Test 1268 cool-flame extinction differs between the spreadsheet (0) and the report (2.563 mm). Report Figure 3 caption says 12% O2 while its data box gives 0.216

name: DAFT / DAFT-2 (Dust and Aerosol measurement Feasibility Test)
objective: Dust and aerosol measurement, not combustion; listed in the mission brief to mark it out of scope
sources: NASA Space Apps mission brief
